opportunities.title: Triple-A's $11.8M Treasury Breach: The Playbook Never Changes
opportunities.why_now: A confirmed treasury-wallet breach with an $11.8M loss just landed, and the mechanics almost certainly rhyme with every prior 'hot wallet as treasury' failure.
opportunities.angle: Incident teardown: reconstruct the attack chain, name the control gap (key custody/multisig threshold), end with the checklist every project ignores until it's too late.

opportunities.title: Three Exploits, One Week: Triple-A, Garden Finance, WEMIX — What Actually Broke
opportunities.why_now: Three distinct incidents (treasury wallet, HTLC bridge, game-token contract) hit within 48 hours, giving a rare clean sample size to compare root causes side by side.
opportunities.angle: Comparative security roundup: one paragraph per incident on the exact failure mode (custody vs. HTLC logic vs. contract permissions), then a unifying thesis on what 2026 attackers are actually targeting.

opportunities.title: SparkKitty Is Back: The App Store Malware Hunting Your Seed Phrase
opportunities.why_now: Seed-phrase-stealing malware slipping past Apple/Google review is a direct, ongoing threat to retail holders reading this today.
opportunities.angle: Practical security explainer: how SparkKitty operates, what permissions/behaviors to check before installing any wallet-adjacent app, plus a hardware-wallet-first takeaway.

opportunities.title: SummerFi Shuts Down After Seven Years — Another Name for the DeFi Exploit Graveyard
opportunities.why_now: A seven-year-old, presumably battle-tested protocol just cited an exploit as the reason it's closing, undercutting the 'time-tested = safe' narrative.
opportunities.angle: Obituary-style post-mortem: what SummerFi survived vs. what finally killed it, framed as a reminder that longevity isn't a security model.

opportunities.title: Hong Kong Just Measured Bank Quantum Readiness. The Score Was Ugly.
opportunities.why_now: A central bank publishing a hard, low quantum-preparedness number is a rare concrete data point in an otherwise speculative threat conversation.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking security piece: translate the HKMA number into what it means for exchange/custodian key schemes, and why 'quantum is far off' is the same complacency that preceded every other breach on this list.
